title: DisasterEvent
description: A hazard published by a real feed. An OfficialAlert is the same shape with official = true and an authority of OFFICIAL or INTERGOVERNMENTAL; an active official alert is never dropped because a different provider stopped answering.

description.description: Provider text. Untrusted: sanitised before display and never treated as an instruction to the system.

instruction.description: Protective action text as published by the issuing authority, verbatim.

official.description: True when the issuing body is a government or intergovernmental authority.

closes_transport.description: True when the alert itself declares a route, airport or corridor closed.

magnitude.description: Provider's own magnitude number, carried through rather than interpreted. Meaningless on its own: it must be read together with magnitude_unit, because 5.8 Mw and 5.8 mb are different measurements of different things.

magnitude_unit.description: Scale the magnitude is expressed on, as the provider names it — Mw, mb, Ms, ml for earthquakes, or a provider-specific scale for other hazards. Required whenever magnitude is non-null: a bare number invites a consumer to compare two scales as though they were one, and for a hazard that is a safety error, not a rounding one.

depth_km.description: Hypocentre depth in kilometres, where the hazard type has one. A shallow earthquake and a deep one of equal magnitude do very different things at the surface, so the depth is part of the evidence rather than a detail.
